description:
We are TECH-UNJBG, a team of Mechanical Engineering students from Universidad Nacional Jorge Basadre Grohmann (Tacna, Peru). 

We are taking on the 'Flame in Freefall' challenge to analyze microgravity combustion data and improve fire safety in space missions. Our fully formed team combines strong skills in thermodynamics, data analysis, and problem-solving. 

We are driven by a shared passion for space exploration and ready to develop real aerospace solutions.
summary: VIGIA is an SI-powered web dashboard for fire safety in space. Using real NASA data (PSI-117, International Space Station), it shows that the visible flame of an n-heptane droplet goes out at 12.8 s, yet the droplet keeps burning with an invisible cool flame until 45.8 s: 33 s of hidden risk. VIGIA integrates 674 NASA tests (FLEX, CFI, ACME, BASS, SAME-R and SAFFIRE), predicts how a fire will end with 80.5 % accuracy (validated on 261 tests vs. a 68.6 % baseline) and verifies extinction step by step before declaring a fire "out". It is designed for Moon and Mars bases, which will use higher oxygen at lower pressure and where no partial-gravity fire data exist yet. Team TECH-UNJBG, Tacna, Peru. Website: https://tech-unjbg.github.io/vigia/
